gate: Does a primary source publish an independent critical fractional-dissipation exponent for 2D Boussinesq (or its vorticity-stream equivalent)?
gate_answer_detail: NO for the quantity solver/fractional_boussinesq.py holds. Stated at full precision because a bare 'no' would be wrong in the other direction: (1) a published exponent named 'critical fractional dissipation' for 2D Boussinesq EXISTS and is alpha+beta = 1, with a ladder of sufficient conditions descending to alpha > 2/3 on that line, and its vorticity-stream equivalent is stated too (at alpha+beta = 1 the problem 'boils down to' critical gSQG); (2) it is NOT COMPARABLE to our s_c -- it is the exponent at which the EQUATION'S SCALING stops preserving the controlling norm, while s_c = 1/(2 beta) is the exponent at which dissipation overtakes ONE SPECIFIC COLLAPSE, and every published value is a one-sided sufficient condition for global regularity, never an equality; (3) NO primary source anywhere publishes an arrest exponent for the Chen-Hou blowup -- the blowup corpus is inviscid without exception and the dissipation corpus never touches a blowup profile. The exponent remains INTERNALLY-CONSISTENT-ONLY; no claim upgrade, no computation attempted.

papers_read_at_full_text.cite: Stefanov, Wu, Xu, Ye, Global regularity of the 2D fractional Boussinesq equations with subcritical dissipation
papers_read_at_full_text.read: abstract, sec 1 introduction IN FULL (the complete survey of published exponents), reference list
papers_read_at_full_text.quote_question: This naturally leads to the fundamental question: how much dissipation is required to ensure global regularity?
papers_read_at_full_text.quote_definition: Jiu, Miao, Wu, and Zhang [20] discovered that the global regularity problem for (1.1) depends crucially on the value of alpha + beta. In the special case alpha + beta = 1, the Boussinesq regularity problem boils down to the corresponding problem on the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic equation with critical dissipation. This insight led to the classification of alpha+beta into three regimes: the subcritical regime (alpha+beta > 1), the critical regime (alpha+beta = 1) and the supercritical regime (alpha + beta < 1). ... In particular, the global regularity problem for the supercritical regime remains largely out of reach
papers_read_at_full_text.verdict: PUBLISHES a critical exponent RELATION for 2D Boussinesq under fractional dissipation -- alpha+beta = 1 -- and it is NOT the quantity we hold. Its criticality is a well-posedness/scaling threshold inherited by reduction to critical gSQG; ours is the exponent at which dissipation overtakes a PARTICULAR collapse rate and depends on the Chen-Hou profile's constants, which enter nowhere in this ladder. Every published number is a one-sided SUFFICIENT condition for regularity -- an upper bound on any arrest threshold -- so none can be equated to s_c even in principle

papers_read_at_full_text.cite: J. Chen, Singularity formation and global well-posedness for the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda equation with dissipation
papers_read_at_full_text.read: abstract, sec 1.1 (prior results with dissipation), sec 1.2 'Scaling and the critical dissipation' IN FULL, sec 1.3, sec 1.4 Theorems 1.1-1.5 and Remarks 1.2-1.7. Leg 65 read this paper for the weighted-ell^1 claims and leg 45 for computer assistance; this is the first pass to read it FOR THE DISSIPATION EXPONENT
papers_read_at_full_text.quote_definition: Suppose that L = Lambda^gamma in (1.1) for some gamma in [0, 2]. Then the solution of (1.1) enjoys the following scaling property: ... We will show that for several classes of initial data, ||omega||_{L^1} is conserved. In these cases, a simple scaling analysis shows that L = Lambda corresponds to the critical dissipation. For (1.1) with a <= -1, we will show that the equation possesses a-priori L^{|a|} estimate, ... which makes Lambda^gamma with gamma = |a|^{-1} the critical dissipation with respect to the natural scaling of the equation.
papers_read_at_full_text.quote_blowup: (Finite time blow-up for a close to 1/2). Consider (1.1) with L omega = -omega_xx. There exists delta > 0 such that for a in (1/2 - delta, 1/2 + delta), 0 <= nu <= 1, (2.1) develops a self-similar singularity in finite time for some C_c^infty initial data.
papers_read_at_full_text.verdict: The ONE paper found anywhere publishing a critical dissipation exponent for a Hou-Luo-family object -- and it is 1D, and it is AGAIN the scaling quantity, derived from which Lebesgue norm the equation's scaling preserves rather than from any blowup profile's collapse rate. Decisively, Chen proves blowup WITH THE FULL LAPLACIAN (gamma = 2, i.e. s = 1 in our convention) for a ~ 1/2, ABOVE his own critical line gamma_c = 1: he does not treat gamma_c as an arrest threshold at all. Reading his gamma_c as comparable to our s_c would manufacture a contradiction out of two correct statements about different quantities

arithmetic_reading.ratio_is_vacuous: alpha_equiv / 1 = 1/beta identically, by the definition s_c = 1/(2 beta). Comparing our number to the alpha+beta=1 line recovers beta and nothing else. That is the precise sense in which a check against a published value is unavailable: the only published line is the one our formula reproduces trivially
arithmetic_reading.far_field_coincidence_is_internal: alpha_equiv = 0.34240 coincides with |c_omega/c_l| to all digits, as collapse_exponent_from_rescaling's docstring predicts (alpha = -1/beta). Internal, not a check
arithmetic_reading.one_weak_external_consistency_statement: Hmidi-Keraani-Rousset prove global regularity at alpha = 1, beta = 0. Our law predicts arrest for alpha > 0.34240, hence regularity at alpha = 1: CONSISTENT, with the published datum sitting a factor 2.9206 above our threshold. One-sided and weak -- it would pass for any s_c < 0.5 -- but it is the only contact between our number and a published one, and it is not a contradiction. A margin, not a validation
arithmetic_reading.where_a_real_check_would_come_from: a published statement of the form 'the Chen-Hou / Hou-Luo self-similar blowup persists for (-Delta)^s with s < s*', for the SAME profile. None exists at the date of this pass. Our alpha_equiv = 0.34240 sits inside the supercritical regime alpha+beta < 1 that 2606.03680 sec 1 calls 'largely out of reach', so the absence is STRUCTURAL, not an oversight

residual_risk: absence at this depth is not proof. Three directions classified but not read at full text: (i) the paywalled Taylor & Francis anisotropic-critical paper (10.1080/00036811.2026.2685067), whose title promises 'blow-up criteria' -- but CRITERIA are conditional statements, not threshold exponents; (ii) arXiv:2605.16322, a 2026 Hou-Luo-type boundary-JET system, a different system from 2D Boussinesq; (iii) the non-arXiv Boussinesq regularity literature, which 2606.03680's reference list surveys and which contains no blowup-arrest statement by that survey's own account. None of the three could supply a value for the Chen-Hou profile, which is what the gate needs
